The one critical, at all three breakpoints, was that the five tile photographs were never fetched. That turned out to be fixable:

**Assets unblocked.** The original asset pass hit `429` on Figma's `/v1/images` render endpoint after 5 downloads and never retried. That endpoint responds now. I read the `imageRef` hashes off the five rect nodes to confirm the fills, then rendered each rect at `scale=2` as JPEG - which returns exactly the Figma rect crop (2x each layer box: 1458×846, 816×1088, 1076×808, 984×1312, 1674×2232) instead of the 5-9MB source originals. Saved as `how-it-works-01..05.jpg` in the assets dir.

**Wired in with responsive crops.** Each photo is a Figma rect *larger* than its tile sitting at a negative offset (729×423 at -13,0 in a 546×404 tile, etc.) - I verified all five against their absolute bounding boxes, which reproduce the 24px inter-tile gaps exactly. The spec states those as px `object-position`, but px only holds at 404px tall, so each crop is stored as rect-size/tile-size and offset/tile-size percentages fed through four custom properties into a new `.crop` rule in the section CSS module. The framing survives the tile shrinking to `62vw` on mobile.

**Measurement delta.** The "2280px wider" on `Images [181:764]` was the id sitting on the two-run marquee track (2 × 2256px) rather than on one run. The duplicate run is required for the seamless loop, so I moved the id onto the first run and tagged each tile's Image frame, rect fill and chip frame with their own ids.

I deliberately did not re-apply iteration 2's white-ring/reduced-motion changes - those are what the regression notice reverted. Typecheck is clean for this section and eslint passes; the only `tsc` error in the tree is in `the-fleet-roadmap.client.tsx`, another agent's file mid-edit.
